paragraphs: Rav Huna son of Rava: [Bava Kamma 72a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.72a.6).
Rav Chaviva son of Rava: [Avodah Zarah 34a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.34a.8).
Rav Yosef son of Rava (without further designation): Berakhot 13b (compare [Berakhot 13b:21](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.13b.21)).
Rav Mesharshiya son of Rava (without further designation): [Chullin 50a:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.50a.14).[^3]
Rav Sama son of Rava: [Bava Metzia 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.42b.14). Rabbah son of Rava: [Eruvin 93b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.93b.6).[^2]

notes.text: This is a patronymic list, not proof that all listed Rava forms denote one person or that all named sons share a single father. Full supplied Rav Rava and Rabbah forms remain distinct.

The two Eruvin notices name Acha and Rabbah separately. The latter is found in the consulted 93b, beside Hyman’s 93a. In Shabbat the patronymic bar Rava is an alternate reading. The list collects separate notices.

At Berakhot 13b, the consulted text names Rav Yosef son of Rabbah, whereas Hyman lists him under Rava. In Chullin, Rava calls Rav Mesharshiya his son and praises his knowledge of terefot. These statements concern separate notices.
